questions.question: What is the Sidecar pattern?

options.text: A helper container deployed alongside the main application container to provide supporting features

questions.explanation: Sidecar: auxiliary container co-located with main app. Shares network/storage. Provides: logging, monitoring, security, networking. Main app unaware of sidecar. Foundation of service mesh (Envoy, Istio).

questions.question: What is the main benefit of the Sidecar pattern?

options.text: Separates cross-cutting concerns from application code without modifying the app

questions.explanation: Sidecar benefits: separation of concerns (app focuses on business logic), language-agnostic (sidecar works with any app), independent updates, consistent infrastructure across services. No app code changes needed.

questions.question: What are common use cases for sidecars?

options.text: Logging, monitoring, service mesh proxy, security, configuration management

questions.explanation: Sidecar use cases: log collection (Fluentd), metrics (Prometheus exporter), service mesh proxy (Envoy), TLS termination, config sync, secret injection, health checking. Infrastructure concerns externalized.

questions.question: How does a sidecar communicate with the main application?

options.text: Localhost networking, shared volumes, or IPC—they share the same pod/host

questions.explanation: Sidecar communication: same pod = shared localhost (127.0.0.1). Shared volumes for files. Low latency. App calls localhost:port, sidecar intercepts. Transparent to application in many cases.

questions.question: What is Envoy proxy and how does it relate to sidecars?

options.text: A high-performance proxy commonly deployed as a sidecar for service mesh functionality

questions.explanation: Envoy: L7 proxy by Lyft. Deployed as sidecar. Handles: load balancing, circuit breaking, retries, observability, TLS. Foundation of Istio, AWS App Mesh. De facto service mesh data plane.

questions.question: What is the resource overhead of sidecars?

options.text: Each sidecar consumes CPU and memory, multiplied across all service instances

questions.explanation: Sidecar overhead: each instance has sidecar. 100 pods = 100 sidecars. Envoy: ~50MB RAM, some CPU. At scale: significant. Trade-off: operational benefits vs resource cost. Consider sidecar-less alternatives.

questions.question: How does Kubernetes support the Sidecar pattern?

options.text: Multiple containers in a pod share network namespace and can share volumes

questions.explanation: Kubernetes pods: multiple containers share network (localhost), can share volumes. Perfect for sidecars. Init containers for setup. Sidecar containers (K8s 1.28+) for proper lifecycle management.

questions.question: What is sidecar injection?

options.text: Automatically adding sidecar containers to pods, typically via admission webhooks

questions.explanation: Sidecar injection: Istio/Linkerd automatically inject proxy sidecars. Kubernetes admission webhook intercepts pod creation, adds sidecar container. No manual configuration per service. Namespace-level enablement.

questions.question: What happens if a sidecar fails?

options.text: Depends on configuration—may affect main app if sidecar handles critical functions like networking

questions.explanation: Sidecar failure impact: if sidecar handles networking (service mesh), app can't communicate. If logging sidecar fails, app continues but loses logs. Design for graceful degradation. Health checks, restarts.

questions.question: Sidecar vs library: when to use each?

options.text: Sidecar: language-agnostic, independent updates; Library: lower latency, simpler deployment

questions.explanation: Sidecar: polyglot environments, independent versioning, no app changes. Library: lower overhead, simpler (no extra container), tighter integration. Netflix: libraries. Google/Lyft: sidecars. Depends on context.

questions.question: What is the Ambassador pattern related to sidecars?

options.text: A sidecar that proxies network connections from the main container to external services

questions.explanation: Ambassador: sidecar handles outbound connections. Main app connects to localhost, ambassador proxies to external service. Handles: retries, circuit breaking, service discovery. App simplified, ambassador handles complexity.

questions.question: Your team has services in Java, Python, and Go. How do you add consistent observability across all?

options.text: Deploy observability sidecar that collects metrics/logs regardless of application language

questions.explanation: Polyglot observability: sidecar solution. Deploy same sidecar (e.g., OpenTelemetry collector) with each service. Collects metrics, traces, logs uniformly. Language-agnostic. Consistent dashboards across all services.
